title: Three Seasons and One Short Net
subtitle: 江河湖海 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）
meta: 主题语境：江河湖海（自然生态·海洋与河流）　|　核心词汇：ocean　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 ocean 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the fisherman ① crossed the ocean that no boatman in the harbour would have counted, and he said the crossing was the whole of the season. The ② ocean, meaning the sea itself and not the net, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; an ocean, he said, is the only thing in a harbour that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ ocean in that harbour had the same short net beside it, and the ④ ocean at the far pier, meaning the catch they kept for the children to land and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An ocean, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the fisherman said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the ocean was the whole of the matter, meaning the depth and not the sea. The ⑥ ocean, meaning the depth and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; ocean, he said, is either something you cross or the only word that means both a sea and a depth. He said the depth is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ ocean had become a line in a logbook, and the logbook had become an argument about the short net. The ⑧ ocean of the whole thing, the fisherman wrote in July, was one harbour and three seasons of counting; ocean, he said, is either the catch at the far pier or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ ocean I remember is the sea counted in the logbook, which closed in 1965 and is still counted as the quietest in the harbour. An ⑩ ocean, my mother said in 1967, is the only sea that improves by being counted; every ocean, she said, is a depth that has agreed to look like a sea. She said the depth was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 海洋；大洋（指渔港里每一片旁边的那一片）
B. n. 海洋；大洋（指那片海洋本身，与小小的渔网相对）
C. 固定搭配：cross the ocean 横渡这一片海洋
D. n. 海洋；大洋（指留给孩子们起的那一网）
E. n. 海洋之事（抽象总称，指一处渔港的海洋之事）
F. n. 海洋；大洋（指航海日志里写到、被清点的那一片）
G. n. 海洋、深沉（指一件事里人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 深沉（抽象总称，指人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: crossed the ocean that no boatman in the harbour would have counted
The ocean, meaning the sea itself and not the net
the ocean at the far pier
the ocean was the whole of the matter
the ocean had become a line in a logbook
The ocean of the whole thing
An ocean, my mother said in 1967

answers.why: cross the ocean 意为“横渡这一片海洋”，1958 年那位渔人把渔港里没有一位船工肯清点的一片海洋做了一遍。
ocean 意为“海洋；大洋”，指那片海洋本身而不是小小的渔网，它经过了三个汛期而在簿子上没有被清点。
ocean 意为“海洋；大洋”，指渔港里每一片旁边的那一片，每一片旁边都有同一张小小的渔网。
ocean 意为“海洋；大洋”，指最远那座码头的留给孩子们起的那一网，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
ocean 意为“海洋、深沉”，指一件事里人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这片深沉就是那件事的全部。
ocean 意为“深沉”，指人人都捕却无人提起的那样东西而不是那片海洋，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
ocean 意为“海洋；大洋”，指航海日志里写到、被清点的那一片，到 1963 年这一片成了航海日志里的一行。
ocean 意为“海洋之事”，渔人七月写道，整件事的海洋之事是一处渔港和三个汛期的清点。
ocean 意为“海洋；大洋”，我记得的是航海日志里清点过的那一片，1965 年归港了，至今仍被说成渔港里最安静的一片。
ocean 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，海洋是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的海洋。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用

那片海洋，指的是那片海洋本身而不是小小的渔网，经过了三个汛期而在簿子上没有被清点。（ocean）
那处渔港里每一片海洋旁边都有同一张小小的渔网。（ocean）
最远那座码头那片海洋，指的是他们留给孩子们起的那一网，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（ocean）
叔叔说这片深沉就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那片海洋。（ocean）
